dispatch_instance_contended.description: A policy admission found the instance's admission guard taken by a keyless observe or probe for its whole short retry (about 100 ms). The dispatch intent already written is rejected at info; the candidate may run again from next_eligible_unix_ms, about one second later.
dispatch_instance_contended.common_causes: A read-only observation or a monitor probe of the instance was in progress when the dispatch was admitted.
dispatch_instance_contended.handling: Nothing to repair. The next policy evaluation dispatches the candidate once the observation has finished.

dispatch_instance_cooldown.description: A policy candidate met an instance whose takeover cooldown still runs after a previous owner ended without closing; the candidate is deferred with a wake at next_eligible_unix_ms, the cooldown's end. Nothing is written for it.
dispatch_instance_cooldown.common_causes: actingd was killed or crashed while it held a lease on the instance, and the new owner started less than the takeover cooldown (6 s by default) ago.
dispatch_instance_cooldown.handling: Nothing to repair. The candidate is evaluated again when the cooldown ends.

dispatch_instance_held.description: A policy candidate, or its admission, met an instance that a claim holds or that an eligible claim waits for (holder_kind names the holder, or the waiting claim that receives the key next; count is the number of eligible waiting claims). The candidate is deferred with no wake, or its intent is rejected at info; the policy driver evaluates again when a lease is released, transferred or expires.
dispatch_instance_held.common_causes: A stuck-recovery ladder, a startup package, an operator command or a direct task run holds the instance, or waits for it, when a dispatch is due.
dispatch_instance_held.handling: Nothing to repair. The candidate runs after the holder releases the instance; actingctl status shows lease_active and queued_request_count meanwhile.

held_timeout.description: A held start (actingd --install-held) received no release before its held deadline. The installation transition fails with admission closed; the operation is install_transition.
held_timeout.common_causes: The installer stopped, timed out or lost its connection before it sent the release.

install_startup_shut_down.description: A held start (actingd --install-held) ended because a shutdown request for its owner was accepted before it was released; the operation is install_transition. It is a formal stop: the watchdog holds it and never restarts it.
install_startup_shut_down.common_causes: An installer, the console or actingctl request-shutdown stopped an owner that waited for its release.

install_startup_stopped.description: A held or released start stopped before it finished preparing because the Runtime latched a failure meanwhile; the operation is install_transition. The latched failure is the outcome's caused_by link in the ledger (ledger revision 3), and the tokens cause=<code> cause_operation=<operation> on the FATAL line and in the transition's status fact. A restart may succeed, so the watchdog considers a start.
install_startup_stopped.common_causes: A ledger write that failed on a request thread while the start was preparing.

maintenance_artifact_material_unavailabl.description: ledger-maintenance refused a root whose artifact retention is not settled: on a formal root an eviction intent without its outcome (pending_evictions counts the artifacts), on a Segment root any recorded eviction.
maintenance_artifact_material_unavailabl.common_causes: A hard stop (power loss, forced reboot) between an eviction intent and its outcome; a Segment root that already records evictions.
maintenance_artifact_material_unavailabl.handling: Start actingd once on the root so that startup recovery finishes the pending eviction, then run the maintenance operation again.

material_read_missing.description: A material read found no file for an artifact that has no eviction proof; the read result is missing and the Runtime records nothing.
material_read_missing.common_causes: A frame deleted by hand from the state root's artifacts folder.
material_read_missing.handling: Nothing to repair in the Runtime; the frame is gone. Read another frame, or restore the file from a copy if it is still needed.

policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled.description: A start could not settle a scheduled run: the host's recovery or the ledger refused its settlement (failure_code is the refusal's code). The start carries on: the run's dispatch stays open, out of the active workloads, and the run's instance is paused with this code as the pause reason, so no new dispatch meets the open one. Recorded once per start, under the run's links, which carry the run id; lease_id is present when the dispatch has one lease grant.
policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled.common_causes: A run whose recorded facts do not fit any settlement the Runtime knows, for example a ledger written by a defect in an earlier version.
policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled.handling: Report it with the run id and failure_code: the open dispatch needs a fix in the Runtime. After looking, lift the instance's scheduling pause (resume scheduling for the instance) to let other tasks dispatch there again; the open dispatch itself stays open until a version that can settle it starts.

policy_settlement_release_recovered.description: A start found a scheduled run whose dispatch has no outcome and whose lease has no lease.released under its run links, wrote the missing release (effect not_performed) and settles the run once: from its terminal when it has one, otherwise as interrupted (policy_settlement_interrupted), so the dispatch is closed; the first such interruption of its pair in a row is lifted by the same start. Recorded once, under the run's links, which carry the run id.
policy_settlement_release_recovered.common_causes: The Runtime ended between a run's task terminal and its lease end (for example inside a failed run's hand-off to its stuck-recovery ladder), in the middle of a run (a reboot or a killed process), or after a scheduled dispatch's lease grant and before its run's first task event.
policy_settlement_release_recovered.handling: Nothing to repair: the run counts as its terminal says, or as interrupted when it has none. A second interruption of the same pair in a row keeps the pair paused until its package changes, as for any interrupted settlement.

policy_settlement_dispatch_left_open.description: After a start's reconciliation, a scheduled dispatch (its task's procedure is one the policy driver runs as a scheduled run) still has no outcome. The start settles every scheduled dispatch it can; this one stays open, and a later dispatch on its instance may be refused as a conflict. Recorded once per start, under the run's links, which carry the run id; lease_id is present when the dispatch has one lease grant.
policy_settlement_dispatch_left_open.common_causes: The run's instance is no longer in the configuration, or the run's lease ended in more than one way (for example two transfers).
policy_settlement_dispatch_left_open.handling: Report it with the run id: the open dispatch needs a fix in the Runtime. When the instance was removed from the configuration, adding it back lets the next start settle the run.

proposal_report_unavailable.description: A proposal or strategic report request was refused because a verified report artifact could not be read back: a proposal's cited report, or the stored report that a strategic report with identical content would reuse.
proposal_report_unavailable.common_causes: The report file was deleted by hand or damaged after it was recorded.
proposal_report_unavailable.handling: Restore the report file from a copy if it is still needed. Otherwise prepare a strategic report whose content differs (for example a later as-of position), which records a new report artifact, and cite that report.

recovery_ladder_key_lost.description: A stuck-recovery ladder found, at a holding check, that it no longer holds its instance's key. It cancels its continuation, records the current rung failed with this reason and finishes exhausted at warning, without an error point.
recovery_ladder_key_lost.common_causes: In practice only a stopping host; otherwise a step that overran its own bound so the key lapsed.
recovery_ladder_key_lost.handling: Nothing to repair: the instance is handed on, and the next trigger starts a new ladder.

runtime_restart_required.description: An instance worker panicked again before it finished one payload after it was rebuilt from an earlier panic (spec section 7). The Runtime is marked fatal and actingd exits with this outcome; each panic was recorded as panic_caught under its payload's own failure category.
runtime_restart_required.common_causes: A defect that panics on every payload of one instance.
runtime_restart_required.handling: actingd is restarted by its supervisor; report the panic_caught records with the build.

release_timeout.description: A released start did not finish preparing before its release deadline. The installation transition fails with admission closed; the operation is install_transition.
release_timeout.common_causes: A slow preparation, such as the startup recovery of a long ledger.

strategic_evidence_unavailable.description: A strategic report request was refused because one of its verified evidence artifacts could not be read back.
strategic_evidence_unavailable.common_causes: An evidence frame or file was deleted by hand or damaged after it was recorded.
strategic_evidence_unavailable.handling: Cite evidence whose files still exist, then submit the report again.

frame_retention_remove_failed.description: The frame cleaner could not delete a due frame at its object key for another reason than a held or absent file. The frame stays, is not tried again by this process, and is tried again after a restart.
frame_retention_remove_failed.common_causes: Access to the state root's artifacts folder denied by the file system or by security software.
frame_retention_remove_failed.handling: Check the file's permissions and any program that blocks it, then restart actingd so that the cleaner tries again.

frame_retention_move_failed.description: The frame cleaner could not move an error or Lab frame into its kept folder (entry, relative to the state root) for another reason than a held or absent file; the frame stays at its object key, is not tried again by this process, and is tried again after a restart.
frame_retention_move_failed.common_causes: A file where the kept date folder or leaf should be; access to the state root's kept folder denied; a full disk.
frame_retention_move_failed.handling: Remove whatever blocks the kept folder named by entry, then restart actingd so that the cleaner tries again.

frame_retention_counter_failed.description: A frame moved into its kept folder, but the move counter kept/.moves (entry) could not be written, so other processes may find moved frames only at their next walk of the kept folders, within 60 s. Reported once per process.
frame_retention_counter_failed.common_causes: A folder or a read-only file where kept/.moves should be; access to the kept folder denied.
frame_retention_counter_failed.handling: Remove whatever occupies kept/.moves so that a file can be written there; the next move writes the counter again.

emulator_restart_stop_failed.description: An operator emulator restart (a Stop phase and then a Start phase under one instance admission guard) whose Stop was not confirmed: the provider's shutdown failed (stop_result names the device stage) or its readiness wait expired (stop_result wait_timeout). After an expired wait the Start phase still runs (start_dispatched true); after any other Stop failure it does not. The restart fails whatever its Start did, and the record carries the last observed state; it is the request's one failure record and its receipt terminal, written after the Start phase when one ran. The control failure behind it (emulator_control_wait_timeout or emulator_control_failed) is the outcome's caused_by link (ledger revision 3); stop_result is left out when the device stage's last part is not a token of its vocabulary.
emulator_restart_stop_failed.common_causes: The vendor's shutdown of the instance hung, for example its device process stayed after Android stopped (device_process_present true), or MuMuManager refused the shutdown.

emulator_restart_start_failed.description: An operator emulator restart whose Stop phase was confirmed and whose Start phase failed: the provider's launch failed or its readiness wait expired. The state read after the failure is applied (a stopped instance is pending, with device.connected false) and carried on the record, which is the request's one failure record and its receipt terminal. The control failure behind it (emulator_control_wait_timeout or emulator_control_failed) is the outcome's caused_by link (ledger revision 3); stop_result is left out when the device stage's last part is not a token of its vocabulary.
emulator_restart_start_failed.common_causes: The instance did not boot within the start's readiness wait, or MuMuManager refused the launch.

emulator_stop_process_unverified.description: A Stop was confirmed by MuMuManager info alone: the process listing that checks that no vendor device process of the instance is left failed or passed its bound, so device_process_present is unknown. Recorded once per Stop under the request's links (a stuck-recovery ladder's on its emulator-restart rung), before command.validated.
emulator_stop_process_unverified.common_causes: The process listing (PowerShell) did not answer within its bound under host load, or could not start.

clock_slot_refused.description: A persistent gate refused a due clock slot of a policy task on an instance (task_id, alias): a budget (policy_budget_exhausted, with budget_dimension), a closed activity window, a task paused by failure suspension, or the configuration (the task disabled for the instance, a missing capability or activity profile). gate_code is the gate's own code. Recorded once per task, instance and occurrence (occurrence_unix_ms) as a goal_missed planning signal whose fact_code is this code followed by key=value tokens and whose signal_id is signal:clock_slot:refused:<sha256 of task, alias and occurrence>. window_end_unix_ms is the end of the activity window open at the refusal, next_eligible_unix_ms the first time the pair may be admitted again, next_occurrence_unix_ms the next clock occurrence.
clock_slot_refused.common_causes: A daily or window budget already used that day, often by an owed run that served the previous day's slot; the activity window closed before the slot could run; the task is paused after repeated failures; the task is disabled for the instance, or the instance lacks the operation or a matching activity profile.
clock_slot_refused.handling: Compare next_eligible_unix_ms with next_occurrence_unix_ms: below it, the slot runs later in the same or the next window; at or above it, the slot is lost to the next occurrence. Change the catalog (budget, slot times, activity window) or the instance configuration if the slot must run.

clock_slot_deferred.description: A transient gate held back a due clock slot of a policy task on an instance (task_id, alias). An operator scheduling pause is recorded at first sight; a queue wait (a held instance, a retry backoff, an activity interval or any other deferral) or an unavailable instance only at an evaluation where the pair's activity window is closed, that is once the wait outlasted the window. gate_code is the gate's own code. Recorded once per task, instance and occurrence as a goal_missed planning signal whose signal_id is signal:clock_slot:deferred:<sha256 of task, alias and occurrence>; it carries the same values as clock_slot_refused. A later refusal of the same occurrence because its window closed is not recorded.
clock_slot_deferred.common_causes: An operator paused scheduling across the slot; another claim held the instance until the activity window closed; the instance stayed unavailable until the window closed.
clock_slot_deferred.handling: Nothing to repair for an operator pause. For a wait that outlasted the window, check what held the instance (actingctl status) or why it stayed unavailable.

clock_slot_owed.description: A policy dispatch selected for a task on an instance (task_id, alias) serves a clock occurrence (occurrence_unix_ms) from before the activity window it was selected in opened (window_start_unix_ms); for a daily-limited task it uses the new day's budget for an earlier slot. first_run is true when the pair had no earlier dispatch; next_occurrence_unix_ms is the next clock occurrence, so a reader can tell whether the run still served this occurrence. Recorded once, at the first cycle that selects the pair for that occurrence, as a goal_missed planning signal whose signal_id is signal:clock_slot:owed:<sha256 of task, alias and occurrence>.
clock_slot_owed.common_causes: The slot fell while the activity window was closed or the Runtime was not running; a gate held the slot back the day before; a catalog was activated with new task ids outside the window.
clock_slot_owed.handling: Nothing to repair for a single owed run. Owed runs every morning together with refusals of the day's own slot mean that the slot's daily budget is displaced: gate the slot with its own timeline window or move it to the window start.
